messages:
Maya: quick brain-dump from the canary sync. proposing an adjudicator layer (lightweight central arbiter) that consumes compact signals and produces deterministic actions. want feedback on tradeoffs.
Evan: curious why a central adjudicator vs fully local policy agents?
Maya: local agents are good for speed but they diverge. adjudicator gives a single source of truth for action ordering and conflict resolution while staying small.
Ravi: main risks: single point of wrongness and latency. can we make it "adjudicator-lite" (stateless merge only) and keep heavy evaluation at edges?
Maya: exactly. edges do heavy scoring; they emit signed signal tuples: `{source, metric, value, samples, sig}`. adjudicator merges, applies policy, emits action events.
Nina: what merge rules? we need deterministic, idempotent semantics. also actions should be reversible.
Maya: plan: each action includes an action_id, origin_score, precedence (service-level, release-level, operator), and expiry. adjudicator orders by (precedence, origin_score, timestamp) and uses CRDT-like last-write-win for same-action_id, but rejects conflicting actions unless higher-precedence.
Evan: nice. operator precedence required for sheriff flow. how do ops force immediate safe state?
ops-bot: NOTE: ops kill-switch exists: `sheriff:force-safe` command. It posts a signed override event to adjudicator.
Ravi: we should cap action rate per release to avoid oscillation. proposal: windowed limits (e.g., max 2 traffic-shifts per 10m) + backoff.
Nina: plus a soft-guard: suggested actions are annotated with expected impact (latency delta, cost delta). adjudicator prefers lower-impact mitigations first if they meet policy.
Maya: policy language idea: small JSONish DSL stored with rollout config. examples: `[{"when": [{"err_rate": ">1%","window":"1m"}], "then": [{"action":"reduce_traffic","pct":50}], "mode":"immediate"}]` and a more composable variant using `all_of` / `any_of`.
Evan: can we compile that DSL to a tiny decision tree so adjudicator eval is O(n signals) and cheap?
Maya: yes. we precompile policies into bytecode that adjudicator evaluates. edges still compute primary metrics.
Luis: testing: we need shadow-run where adjudicator emits actions to `audit` topic only. plus a replayable trace log with hashed payloads for later deterministic replays.
Ravi: add a simulator that takes historical signals and runs policy bytecode to validate false-positive/negative rates before enabling automatic enforcement.
Nina: also add tenant-scoped config: some services get high-safety defaults (manual approval), others opt into auto-remediation.
Maya: follow-ups: (1) write adjudicator merge semantics doc, (2) design DSL minimal grammar + compiler, (3) signal schema (signed, aggregated), (4) simulator + shadow-run plan. I'll open RFC and tag owners.
Evan: I'll take simulator.
Ravi: I'll draft merge semantics + rate-limiter hooks.
Nina: ops UI for sheriff + provenance, I'm on it.
Maya: awesome. propose we flip adjudicator into observe-only for next canary and collect suggested actions for 24h.
ops-bot: Deploy notice: canary rollout 2.7 in us-east started at 10% traffic. link: https://console/redwood/deploys/2400 :eye_in_speech_bubble:
Luis: good. let's collect traces and reconvene after 24h.
Maya: thanks all, will add RFC link once created :rocket:
